_about: Where the two judging runs disagree on whether a light changed or when, the decision and why (28 Oct 2026). Elsewhere run 1 is taken: where the runs differ only in which source's text describes an unchanged light, or in filling the window around a dated change, the timelines are the same.

isle-of-may.why: Edwards (March 1884) still has two fixed lights and Findlay 1887 the 4-flash electric light, with no alteration year: the change falls in 1884-1886, which the overlapping spans mark as uncertain. The usual date (1 Dec 1886) is from outside these witnesses and is not used.

holy-isle.why: The station's own light is fixed green in both editions and in the 1879 report; the red light in Findlay 1887's entry is Lamlash pier's, shown in winter only. The 1887 alteration year (1880) is left unexplained.

north-carr-lv.why: Findlay 1887 calls the light-vessel 'proposed', year 1887; the reports list the station from 1885. The character is the proposed one, from 1887 only; observations there in 1885-86 (if any) are drawn without a light.

calf-rock.why: Not a change of character: the lighthouse was destroyed in the gale of 26 Nov 1881 (Findlay 1887); its span ends in 1881 in both runs.

dursey-island.why: The temporary light that replaced Calf Rock after Nov 1881; the reports list Dursey from 1882, so its span starts in 1882.

north-stack.why: A fog-signal station that 'occasionally' showed a small light (the 1880 report's own words, its only witness); listed in 1880-81 only. Run 1 also gave it a Findlay 1887 span, but Findlay has no row for it.
